r: Said to have built **360 temples** – "the Vengi ruler who built many temples"; built the **Pancharamas**
Founded by him – the **Bhimeswara** temple, an **Eastern Chalukya** monument
**Draksharama Bhimeswara** and **Kumararama Bhimeswara at Samalkot**, the latter in memory of his **son**
A Pancharama, not a Shakti Peetha
A Narasimha shrine, not a Pancharama
Four lie in the Godavari delta, **Amararama** on the **Krishna**
Huge Nandi mandapa; one of the **Trilinga** kshetras

b.x: **Sapta Godavari:** the sacred tank (**pushkarini**) of the **Draksharama Bhimeswara** temple; legend says the Seven Sages brought its water, used for the abhisheka.
**Jananathapura:** Draksharama was also the provincial capital and coronation seat of the Chalukya-Chola viceroys of Vengi.

r: The **Raichur Doab (Raichur Antarvedi)**, between the **Krishna and Tungabhadra**
Fertile black soil and a strategic position = **main cause of the Bahmani–Vijayanagara wars** from **Harihara I's** time
A separate coastal tract contested by Reddis, Velamas, Gajapatis, Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis
Pandya Jatavarman Sundara killed Manumasiddhi II; Kakatiya Ganapatideva defeated
**Vijayanagara** (Aliya Rama Raya killed) vs the **Deccan Sultans** – Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar

b.x: **Berar did not join** the Talikota alliance; after Talikota Golconda took **Kondavidu, Machilipatnam** and the coast, and Vijayanagara moved to **Penugonda**, later Chandragiri.

r: **Qutb Shahi** – Sultan Quli (Bahmani tarafdar of Telangana)
Last ruler **Abul Hasan Tana Shah**, removed by **Aurangzeb (1687)**

b.x: Chronology: Kakatiyas → Kondaveeti Reddis → Vijayanagara → Bahmanis → Gajapatis; the Reddis came **after** the Kakatiyas.

r: The **Musunuri Nayaks** took it back from the Muslims
Musunuris, Reddis and Velamas were **Prataparudra's generals** who rose after 1323
**Anavota Reddy** shifted it from **Addanki to Kondavidu**
Ceded by **Kapaya Nayaka** to Bahmani Muhammad I after his son **Vinayaka** was killed (1361)
Son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi – **first Chalukya-Chola king**
Chola throne **1070**; Vengi **1075** after the death of **Vijayaditya VII**, the last Eastern Chalukya → **united the Chola and Eastern Chalukya crowns**
Sent **72 merchants to China**; built **Kulottunga Cholapuram** (Visakhapatnam); conquered **Kalinga by sea** → **Kalingattuparani** by **Jayangondar**
At **Jananathapura (Draksharama)**, the provincial capital of Vengi
Served after Rajaraja Chodaganga; recalled in **1118** as his father's **co-regent**

b.x: **After Kulottunga:** Andhra became a web of **nadus** under vassals who accepted **Velanadu**, later **Kakatiya**, overlordship; he raised the Velanati, Nellore, Konidena and Pottapi Chodas, Chagis and Kona Haihayas as Mandaleswaras.
**Battle of Manneru:** **Kulottunga II**, sent to Vengi by Vikrama Chola, with the chiefs of **Velanadu, Giripaschima and Konakandravadi** drove out the **Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas**.
**Mitakshara:** by **Vijnaneshwara** at the court of **Vikramaditya VI** – a **commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti**.

r: All castes; not only male members' property
**Madhavacharya (Vidyaranya)** – on the Parashara Smriti; main law book of **Vijayanagara** justice

b.x: Famous jurists: **Vijnaneshwara, Hemadri, Jimutavahana**; **Rajasekhara** was a poet-critic (Kavyamimamsa, Karpuramanjari), not a jurist.
Unequal inheritance among sons: among the **Nambudiri** Brahmins of Kerala only the **eldest son** married within the caste and held the property; the **Nayars** were matrilineal (marumakkathayam).

r: **Vijayalaya**, a **Pallava feudatory at Uraiyur** – captured **Thanjavur** from the **Muttaraiyars** in **850 CE** (9th century)
**Aditya I** (871–907) – defeated the last Pallava **Aparajita** and ended Pallava rule
**Maduraikonda**; Uttaramerur inscriptions; lost **Takkolam (949)** to Rashtrakuta **Krishna III**
Accession began the **golden age**; Brihadeeswara; navy; the **Cholas** the dominant power
Named heir in **1012** – ruled jointly two years; Ganga (1022) and Srivijaya (1025) expeditions
Crowned on the battlefield of Koppam; victory pillar at **Kolhapur**
Defeated by Pandya **Maravarman Kulasekara**; Chola rule ended **1279**
The **Coromandel Coast** and parts of the Deccan (Tungabhadra–Krishna)
**Coromandel** comes from **Cholamandalam**; Tondaimandalam was the Pallava country
**Uraiyur** = earliest (Sangam) Chola capital; Kaveripattinam (Puhar) = Sangam port
Two inscriptions on the temple walls at **Uttaramerur**, a **brahmadeya** village in **Kanchipuram district**, Tamil Nadu
Main source of Chola local government
Constitution of the sabha, **qualifications**, **disqualifications**, mode of election (**kudavolai**), committees, functions and the **right to recall**
Records military feats (Chera navy at Kandalur), not village government
Own at least **1/4 veli** of tax-paying land
Debt defaulters; close relatives of members
Served on a committee in the **past three years**

b.x: **Aug 2025:** the PM cited the Uttaramerur **"ballot pot"** as proof of India's early democratic traditions.
1. Village divided into **30 wards (kudumbus)**; 2. names of eligible persons written on **palm leaves**; 3. put in a **pot (kudam)**; 4. a **young boy** drew the lots in public.
**Term:** **360 days** (one year); removed at once for an offence; a person who served in the last three years was barred.
Uttaramerur committees covered **irrigation, gardens, justice and finance**.

r: Land whose revenue maintained the **village tank**
Land of non-Brahmin peasant proprietors (ur villages)
A **very large village** (an important brahmadeya or nagaram) **administered as a single, separate unit**, outside the nadu

b.x: **Rate:** land revenue normally **1/6 of the produce** (like the Pallavas and Kakatiyas); collected by village assemblies in cash, kind or both; **Rajaraja I's land survey**.
**Remission:** exemptions granted through the **ur**; **Kulottunga I = Sungam Tavirtta Chola** (abolished tolls).

r: Originated at **Aihole (Ayyavolu), Karnataka**; pan-regional and overseas
**Corporation of merchants** in long-distance and overseas trade
Local merchant assembly of a market town

b.x: **Guilds** (shrenis, pugas) had their own code (**bananju-dharma**), symbols and militias, and acted as bankers; as Chola power declined they became **more independent** – they were not confined to local trade.
**Penugonda** (West Godavari) = central trade centre of medieval Andhra; Ayyavole and Manigramam had **18 branches** across Vengi.
Eastern Chalukya **Nakaras** were headed by **Shreshthis**; **Tagara** = trade centre between Kalyan and Vengi.

r: **Land, money and livestock** (cows, sheep for lamps), guild gifts and royal grants of paddy
Buddhist vihara built (**1006**) by the Srivijaya king **Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman**; Rajaraja I granted it Anaimangalam village
Chola embassies reached the **Song** court in **1015** and **1033**; **Kulottunga I** sent **72 merchants** in **1077**
Friendly at first (Chudamani Vihara) → hostile under **Rajendra I** over the China route (1025)
Guild networks carried Chola trade and Dravidian culture across the Bay of Bengal
Main port of the later Cholas; **Chudamani Vihara**
Early (Sangam) Chola port-capital at the **Kaveri** mouth
Arab merchants traded **horses and spices**; the **Anjuvannam** represented foreign merchants

b.x: **Cultural impact on South-East Asia:** India exported **Buddhism, Sanskrit and temple architecture** (Angkor, Borobudur), but **not the hierarchical caste system**.

r: Bronze images already cast in the **Pallava** period (8th–9th c.) – the earliest South Indian bronzes
The **Chola** period (10th–12th c.) produced the finest; queen **Sembiyan Mahadevi** a key patron
Developed under the **Imperial Cholas**; the **greatest creation** of South Indian sthapatis and **masterpiece of Chola bronzes**
Points to the raised foot – liberation
Fusion of male and female principles
**Rajaraja I** appointed about **400 dancing girls** (with musicians and staff, paid by grants) at the Thanjavur temple; hymns of the Alvars and Nayanars sung in temples
"Female servants of God" – unmarried women dedicated to temple service, music and dance
**Jagannath temple, Puri** – its Devadasis (**Maharis**) served its rituals
Chola inscriptions record temple colleges at **Ennayiram** and **Tribhuvani** (near Pondicherry, South Arcot)
South India; **peak under the Cholas**; continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and Hoysalas
"The **Pallavas laid the foundation**, the **Cholas** developed it on a monumental scale"
The mighty **gateways** of South Indian temples
**Shiva** (huge linga; Tripurantaka); granite; vimana **216 ft**; capstone ~**80 tonnes**; largest and tallest in Tamil Nadu
First of its kind in the south
Enlarged by the Cholas; **Chit Sabha** with **108 dance poses**; outside the UNESCO group
Pallava Shore temple → Brihadeeswara → **Gangaikondacholapuram** (latest of the three)
Brihadeeswara ambulatory – Shiva as **Tripurantaka**, **Rajaraja I with guru Karuvur Thevar**; Narthamalai paintings – Shiva and Parvati
**Kamban** (12th c.), at the court of the **Chola** king **Kulottunga III**
**Nambi Andar Nambi**, Rajaraja I's time – 11 volumes; with the Periya Puranam, 12 books
**Shiva** – the only Shiva temple of the three
**Ketamalla**, officer of Vishnuvardhana, c. 1121 (named in the temple's inscriptions)

b.x: **Hoysala monuments:** **Halebid and Belur**; Hampi and Hospet are Vijayanagara.

r: **Vesara** – hybrid, neither fully Nagara nor Dravida (Kandariya Mahadeva is Nagara)
**Stellate (star-shaped)** on a raised **jagati** (~1 m); the plan began under the **Chalukyas**; best preserved at **Keshava, Somanathapura**

b.x: **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** – inscribed **2023** (Belur, Halebid, Somanathapura), together with **Santiniketan**; Ramappa (Palampet) is a separate Kakatiya site (2021); Rani-ki-Vav (2014) and Mahabodhi (2002) were inscribed earlier.

r: **Modern name** of Dwarasamudra; **Hassan** district, Karnataka; means **"old city"** after the Delhi armies sacked it
Most of **Karnataka**, parts of Tamil Nadu
Feudatories of the **Western Chalukyas** (early chief **Nripa Kama II**)
Independent by the **close of the 12th century**; ended at the **beginning of the 14th**
Original name **Bittideva / Bittiga** (from 1108); fought Vikramaditya VI and the Cholas; took **Talakad** from the Cholas → **Talakadugonda**; built Belur (1117)
Fled **Chola** persecution; Vishnuvardhana converted from **Jainism to Vaishnavism** under him; queen **Shantala Devi** stayed Jain
A **Veeragallu** (hero stone) at **Neeragunda** (Arsikere) may settle the date of Vishnuvardhana's death

b.x: Hoysalas, Gahadavalas, Kakatiyas and Yadavas all arose after the early 8th century.

r: Defeated by Pandya **Maravarman Kulasekhara**; Somanathapura built
Beat Yadava Ramachandra's forces (1305); lost to Kakatiya commander **Pedarudru** after 1316; surrendered to Malik Kafur
Constant Hoysala–Yadava wars – **Singhana** defeated the Hoysalas
Ballala III killed by **Ghiyas-ud-din**, Sultan of Madurai, at **Kannanur** (1342–43); Hoysala land passed to **Vijayanagara** (by 1346)
A youth named **Sala** killed a tiger at **Sosevur** (Angadi, Chikkamagaluru district) when his Jain guru **Sudatta** cried **"Hoy, Sala!"** ("Strike, Sala!") – hence **Hoysala**
**Sala fighting a tiger** – carved at Belur and other Hoysala temples (the boar is the Chalukya emblem)
Hill chiefs of the **Malnad** (Western Ghats) – the **Malepas**; title **Malaparolganda** ("lord among the hill chiefs")
**Nripa Kama II → Vinayaditya → Ereyanga → Ballala I → Vishnuvardhana** – all feudatories of the Western Chalukyas of Kalyani
Vishnuvardhana took the old **Western Ganga** capital from the **Cholas**; Belur's Chennakeshava is said to commemorate it
Jain general of Vishnuvardhana who won Talakad and **restored Jain bastis at Shravanabelagola**
Raised c. 981–83 by **Chavundaraya**, minister of the **Western Ganga** king
**Lakshmi Devi, Doddagaddavalli** (1113–14, among the earliest); **Amriteshwara, Amruthapura** (1196, Veera Ballala II)
Rescued the **Chola Rajaraja III** from the Kadava chief **Kopperunchinga** – the Hoysalas became arbiters in Tamil politics
Second capital at **Kannanur Kuppam** (near Srirangam); kingdom later split between **Narasimha III** (Dwarasamudra) and **Ramanatha** (Kannanur)
**Ballala III** moved his base to **Tiruvannamalai**; many historians link Harihara and Bukka, founders of Vijayanagara, to Hoysala service
*Yashodhara Charite*, *Anantanatha Purana*; court poet of **Veera Ballala II**, title **Kavichakravarti**

b.x: **Language:** Hoysala inscriptions are mostly in **Kannada** (some Sanskrit); Kannada literature flourished in both Jain and Virashaiva streams.
**Religion:** Jainism (Gangaraja, queen **Shantala Devi**), **Sri Vaishnavism** (Ramanuja at **Melukote / Tirunarayanapuram**), Shaivism and Virashaivism all had royal patronage.
**Madhvacharya** (1238–1317), founder of **Dvaita**, was born near **Udupi** in Hoysala times; his math at Udupi worships Krishna.

**Temple carving signature:** sculptors **signed their work**; friezes run **elephants (lowest) → lions / horsemen → scrolls → epic scenes**; **Darpana Sundari** (lady with a mirror) is the famous Belur madanika.

r: Sanskrit encyclopaedia by **Hemadri** – on **dharma, rituals, charity, pilgrimage and vratas**
**Shrikaranadhipa** (head of secretariat and records) under **Mahadeva and Ramachandra**
Claimed that **Jaitugi captured and sacrificed Rudra**
Credited to Hemadri – local **black basalt**, dressed stones **interlocked without mortar** (**dry masonry**)
Court musician of **Singhana II**; **Sangita Ratnakara** – base text of both Hindustani and Carnatic music
Court astronomer of Singhana II; **grandson of Bhaskaracharya**; school at **Patan** to teach Bhaskara's works
**Dnyaneshwari** – Marathi commentary on the **Bhagavad Gita**, **1290**, Nevasa, in **Ramachandra's** reign

b.x: Later Bhakti saints Namdev, Tukaram and Ramdas carried Upanishad and Gita ideas into Marathi.

r: From the **Yadu** clan of Krishna (Dvaravati / Dwaraka) – hence "Yadavas"; their own records call them **Seunas**
**Dridhaprahara** (c. 860), capital **Chandradityapura (Chandor, Nashik district)** – feudatory of the **Rashtrakutas**
Gave the name **Seunadesha** (Khandesh – Nashik region); founded **Seunapura** near **Sinnar**
The **Kalachuri usurpation (Bijjala)** at Kalyani weakened the Chalukyas; **Bhillama V** founded the independent kingdom at **Devagiri (1187)**
Hoysalas (south), **Kakatiyas** (east), **Paramaras of Malwa** and **Vaghelas / Chaulukyas of Gujarat** (north), **Shilaharas of Kolhapur** (south-west)
**Singhana II** annexed the **Shilahara kingdom of Kolhapur** and raided Gujarat and Malwa
Of Devagiri – financed his **murder of Jalaluddin Khalji and seizure of the Delhi throne** the same year
Rock-cut, moated hill fort begun under Bhillama V; renamed **Daulatabad** by Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1327)
Yadava-period **panchayatana** Shiva temple in the **Bhumija** style
Local black basalt, dry masonry without mortar; spread across **Marathwada and Vidarbha** – the Yadava heartland
Credited by tradition with popularising the **Modi script** (cursive Marathi); commentary on *Ashtanga Hridaya* (Ayurveda)
Sanskrit grammarian, author of ***Mugdhabodha***; protégé of Hemadri
Also wrote ***Amritanubhav***; **samadhi at Alandi (1296)**; founding saint of the **Varkari** tradition
Devotion to **Vithoba (Vitthal) of Pandharpur**; annual **wari** pilgrimage; saints **Namdev, Janabai, Muktabai, Gora Kumbhar, Chokhamela** – Dnyaneshwar's contemporaries
His hymns are in the **Guru Granth Sahib**
Founded **1267** by **Chakradhar Swami**; worships **Krishna / Dattatreya**; rejects caste and rituals; writes in **Marathi**
Early Yadava inscriptions mostly in **Kannada**; from the 13th century **Marathi** records and literature grow
The **Rashtrakutas** – the Magallu record calls Gundaya and Eriya "Rashtrakuta"; early emblem **Garuda**
Feudatories of the **Kalyani (Western) Chalukyas** – emblem **Varaha** (changed by **Prola I**); title **Mahamandaleswara**, borne by Beta II
Only issued the Magallu grant; never Kakatiya overlords
Samanta (feudatory) 956–1162 → **sovereign 1163–1323**; the Kakatiyas ruled Andhra in the **12th–13th centuries**

b.x: None of these arose in the early 8th century: Hoysalas 10th–11th c., Gahadavalas 11th c., Kakatiyas and Yadavas 12th c.

r: **First mention** of the Kakatiyas – Kakatiya **Gundyana** (Kakara Gundana)
Best genealogy; line begins with **Venna (Venna Bhupati)**
Names **Beta I** as the **first Kakatiya king**; records the accession of **Durga Nripathi**

b.x: **Early base:** **Hanamkonda (Anumakonda) Vishaya**, received by Beta I through his aunt **Viriyala Kamasani**.

r: **Rameswara Pandita** (Mallikarjuna matha, **Srisailam**) → **Beta II**; **Dhruveshwara Pandita** → **Mahadeva**; **Visvesvara Sivacharya** (Golaki Matha) → **Ganapatideva**
**Second dynasty after the Satavahanas** to unite all Telugu lands; "gave a comprehensive form to Andhraism" – the **ultimate design to Andhra culture**
Ruled by the **Kakatiyas** in the 12th–14th c.; the Seunas held the west

b.x: **P.V. Parabrahma Sastry:** **Kannada (Chalukya) rule in Andhra ended** with the establishment of the Kakatiya kingdom.

r: Developed Hanamkonda; Swayambhu temple in Orugallu
**Completed the fort** and **transferred the capital** from Hanumakonda to **Orugallu**; called it **Andhranagari**

b.x: **Ganapatideva** shifted the capital; the Bekkallu inscription (1195) already calls Orugallu **Rudradeva**'s capital, so the shift is also credited to Rudradeva.

r: **Begun by Rudradeva**, completed by Ganapatideva, strengthened by Rudramadevi
Warangal best reflects the Kakatiya contribution to culture – fort, Thousand Pillar temple, Ramappa nearby
**1199–1262** (about **63 years**, the longest); first inscription **Manthena, 26 Dec 1199**
Held captive by Yadava **Jaitugi**; **Recherla Rudra** crushed revolts and installed him
Brought **the whole Telugu area under one rule** after the Satavahanas, from Ganjam to Kanchi
The most powerful Kakatiya – **extended the empire up to Kanchi**
Coastal campaign – general **Mutyalachaundaraya** took **Divi**; married **Narama and Perama**, daughters of **Pinnachodi**; made their brother **Jayapa** **Gajasahani**
With **Choda Tikka** of Nellore killed **Prithviswara** → Velanati kingdom ended (title **Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda**)

Restored **Manumasiddhi II** after the poet **Tikkana** came as envoy; Tikkana dedicated **Nirvachanottara Ramayana** to **Manumasiddhi**
Fought the **Eastern Gangas** for southern Kalinga and Vengi
**Jatavarman Sundara Pandya** beat the Kakatiyas at **Muttukur** (Nellore); **Nellore fell to the Pandyas**

b.x: The **Pithapuram inscription** of Velanati **Prithvisvara** names **Kolleru Lake**.

r: **Ramappa temple** (Recherla Rudra, 1213), **Lakkavaram** and **Ghanapur** tanks, **Ganapavaram** villages, **Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam** (1244)
**Telugu replaced Sanskrit** in inscriptions from his reign
Succeeded him, raised as a son (putrika), trained by her mother **Kupama Devi**; married **Veerabhadra** of the **Nidadavolu Eastern Chalukyas**

r: **Marco Polo**, the **Venetian (Italian)** traveller; work **Il Milione / The Travels**

Praised the queen's strict and just rule and the country's prosperity

**Diamond** mines of the Golconda region; fine textiles
Hot climate; **rice** the only local grain
**Caste organisation** / caste-occupational association – Mahajanulu (Brahmins), Nakaramu (Vaishyas); each elected a head; met in temple mandapams
Merchants of both the Desis, Paradesis and Nanadesis
Licensed for **Pakanadu, Vengi and Hanumakonda** (Tripurantakam inscription, 1282)

b.x: **Guild head:** **Setti / Sreshthi**; guilds had seals, emblems and militia and acted as bankers; there was **no royal monopoly** over trade.

r: Linked Motupalli and the salt towns to **Ballari** via Kurnool
Chief inland route Kanchi → Nellore → Warangal → **Ayodhya**
Kakatiyas controlled routes between the **Deccan interior and the eastern coast**

b.x: **Kridabhiramamu:** Telugu play by **Vinukonda Vallabharaya** describing life in **Orugallu (Warangal)**.

r: **Recherla (Racherla) Rudra**, general of **Ganapatideva** (not a Kakatiya king); title Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya
**1213 CE** (1162 is the Thousand Pillar temple)
Rudreswaralayam; deity Shiva as **Ramalingeswara**; named after its **sculptor Ramappa**
Single-shrine (**ekakuta**) temple on a star-shaped platform, also described as **Monolithic (Ekasila)**; the Trikuta is the Thousand Pillar temple
Also built by **Recherla Rudra** (1213), in Ganapatideva's reign

**Star-shaped** platform; **floating bricks** in the vimana; **sandbox foundation**.
**Madanika** bracket figures in dance poses; **28** elephant-lion (Gajakesari) figures.
**Painted ceilings** with Ramayana–Mahabharata scenes – Ramappa is a site of **Kakatiya paintings**.

r: **Trikuta** (three shrines) on a star-shaped platform; Chalukyan influence
Built by a minister's wife, not by the early Kakatiya monarchs
**Prasuti griha (maternity home)** and hospital at **Mandadam**, **Rudramadevi's** reign

**Gaja Sahini** (head of the elephant corps) of **Ganapatideva**

b.x: **Nritta Ratnavali** covers **Marga** (classical) and **Desi** (folk) dance and describes **Perini**; the **Ramappa dance sculptures** were carved on its principles.

r: Warrior dance of **male warriors before battle**, invoking Shiva, to drum beats; postures carved at Ramappa
**Nataraja Ramakrishna**, from Nritta Ratnavali and the **Ramappa / Thousand Pillar** sculptures
Recherla feudatories; **Kakatiya mural paintings** – led to the **Lepakshi** style

b.x: **Kakatiya paintings:** at **Pillalamarri** and on the Ramappa ceilings.

**Vidyadhikari** (education officer) under **Pedakomati Vema Reddi**; composed his Sanskrit inscriptions
**Kavi Sarvabhauma**; also Andhra Bhasha Naishadhabhava, Sarvavidya Parangata

Life of the **Palnadu** people; dvipada on the **Palnadu war of 1182** (battle of Karempudi)

b.x: **Madanavilasabanam** is by Naganatha, of Anavota's court.
